messages:
alex klein: Hey team, customer (acme-prod) hitting intermittent 429s during a traffic spike. They reported a ~2k req/min burst for ~30s and we see matching 429s. Need repro evidence (request IDs, response headers, curl reproducer) + debug bundle.

maria ramos: Which environment? hosted or dedicated? Do we have sample request IDs and the response headers?

alex klein: Hosted (api.redwood.ai), customer says it started after a batch job kicked off. Sample response header from their client: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 14:02:11 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 123
x-rw-rlimit-limit: 1200
x-rw-rlimit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rlimit-reset: 14
x-request-id: req_abc12345
```
Response body: `{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit","code":429},"request_id":"req_abc12345"}`

samir patel: Can you also paste the client-side timeline? We need to know whether they retried aggressively (no jitter/backoff). Also which API key was used (prefix ok, no full key).

alex klein: Client timeline from their engineer: 
- 14:01:50 - batch started, ~500 concurrent processes
- 14:02:05 - spike to ~2200 rpm for ~35s
- 14:02:11 - first 429 observed (req_abc12345)
- 14:02:46 - traffic back to baseline
They supplied req ids: req_abc12345, req_abc12346, req_abc12378. Token prefix: `sk-acme-prod_`

jordan lee: Please ask them to run a quick curl repro and include `-v` to capture headers and `--trace-ascii` to capture timing. Example to send them: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-prod_<REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"status"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Make them replace the token and paste the full output including `x-request-id`.

ops-bot: Observed: account=acme-prod tier=hosted burst_window=60s limit=1200rpm detected_spike=2200rpm duration=35s top_ip=203.0.113.45

support-bot: Server logs (filtered) around 14:02:10: 
```
[2025-06-10T14:02:09Z] INFO request=req_abc12344 ip=203.0.113.45 status=200 latency_ms=12
[2025-06-10T14:02:11Z] WARN request=req_abc12345 ip=203.0.113.45 status=429 quota_remaining=0
[2025-06-10T14:02:12Z] WARN request=req_abc12346 ip=203.0.113.45 status=429 quota_remaining=0
[2025-06-10T14:02:13Z] INFO request=req_abc12350 ip=203.0.113.45 status=200 latency_ms=15
```

maria ramos: Looks like single IP source and token hit burst limit. Two asks: (1) request the curl repro + full headers/traces from customer, (2) collect debug bundle for the request ids so we can correlate backend traces.

alex klein: I'll ask them to run the curl and attach the output. Also requested customer to run this internal collector on their side if possible: 
```
rw-support collect-debug --req req_abc12345,req_abc12346 --since 2025-06-10T14:01:00Z --until 2025-06-10T14:05:00Z
```
If they can't run it, we can run server-side collect and attach.

samir patel: Also confirm if they are using shared API keys across many hosts. If multiple hosts share the same key you can easily hit a combined quota.

jordan lee: Temporary mitigation option: apply a per-key throttle on the account or increase burst quota if this is expected traffic. For now propose a short throttle and ask them to add exponential backoff client-side.

alex klein: Customer replied with curl output (redacted token): 
```
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (18.205.93.24) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-prod_<REDACTED>
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 47
< HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
< Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 14:02:11 GMT
< Content-Type: application/json
< x-rw-rlimit-limit: 1200
< x-rw-rlimit-remaining: 0
< x-rw-rlimit-reset: 14
< x-request-id: req_abc12345
< Connection: keep-alive
{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit","code":429},"request_id":"req_abc12345"}
* Closing connection 0
```

maria ramos: Good. Next: attach the rwctl/server debug bundle and I'll correlate traces. If we confirm all requests came from the same IP and same token, this is a quota-usage issue, not a bug in the runtime.

support-bot: Debug bundle created: https://internal.redwood/support/debug/collections/1747092438-acme-prod-429 (expires in 7d)

alex klein: I've sent the repro steps and asked them to add random jitter + exponential backoff. Also requested full tcp trace. I'll follow up with their engineer and update here. :thumbsup:

maria ramos: Thanks, once we have the bundle I'll do the postmortem and recommend policy changes (e.g., per-key burst cap or account-level smoothing).

samir patel: Also flagging for product: consider adding docs for recommended client-side backoff and a diagnostics endpoint that returns per-key quota state. :eyes:

jordan lee: Noted. Closing loop when customer confirms fix.

alex klein: Closing for now — will reopen thread if additional 429s occur. :wave:
notes: repro-step gathering; includes request ids, headers, curl repro, logs, debug bundle link
